Critical Path Method.

Source: R/cpm.R
cpm.Rd

Computes the deterministic schedule of a project_schedule() from its baseline durations: early and late start and finish dates, total and free float, and the critical path. All four precedence-diagramming link types (FS, SS, FF, SF) and lags are supported. With level = TRUE the schedule is resource-leveled against the capacity of each capacity-limited resource.

Usage

cpm(x, level = FALSE)

Arguments

x

A "pra_schedule" object from project_schedule().

level

Logical. Level resources against capacity. Default FALSE.

Value

An S3 object of class "cpm", a list with:

activities

Data frame with one row per activity: id, name, duration, ES, EF, LS, LF, total_float, free_float and critical.

finish

Project finish time.

critical_path

Ids of critical activities in start order.

cost

Deterministic project cost: resource cost plus fixed cost.

leveled

Whether the schedule was resource-leveled.

project

The input schedule.

Objects of this class have print.cpm(), summary.cpm() and plot.cpm() methods.

Details

Forward pass. Activities are visited in topological order. An activity starts at the latest of time zero and the constraint of each incoming link: FS: predecessor finish + lag; SS: predecessor start + lag; FF: predecessor finish + lag - own duration; SF: predecessor start + lag - own duration.

Backward pass. From the project finish (the latest early finish), each activity's late finish is the earliest of the project finish and the mirror constraint of each outgoing link. Total float is late start minus early start, and an activity is critical when its total float is zero (within a small numerical tolerance). Free float is the slack before an activity delays any successor's early dates.

Resource leveling. With level = TRUE activities are scheduled by the serial schedule-generation scheme (Kolisch, 1996): repeatedly take the eligible activity with the smallest unconstrained late start and place it at the earliest time that satisfies its links and keeps every capacity-limited resource within capacity for the activity's whole duration. Float is not meaningful once resources move dates, so late dates and floats are NA and criticality is determined by tracing the driving path backward from the project finish through binding links and through resource hand-offs.

References

Kelley, James E., and Morgan R. Walker. Critical-path planning and scheduling. Papers presented at the December 1-3, 1959, Eastern Joint IRE-AIEE-ACM Computer Conference (1959): 160-173.

Kolisch, Rainer. Serial and parallel resource-constrained project scheduling methods revisited: Theory and computation. European Journal of Operational Research 90.2 (1996): 320-333.

Examples

activities <- data.frame(id = c("A", "B", "C", "D"), duration = c(3, 5, 4, 2))
links <- data.frame(
  source = c("A", "A", "B", "C"),
  target = c("B", "C", "D", "D")
)
sched <- cpm(project_schedule(activities, links))
sched
#> Critical Path Method 
#> Project finish: 10 periods 
#> Critical path: A -> B -> D 
#> 
#>  id duration ES EF LS LF total_float free_float critical
#>   A        3  0  3  0  3           0          0     TRUE
#>   B        5  3  8  3  8           0          0     TRUE
#>   C        4  3  7  4  8           1          1    FALSE
#>   D        2  8 10  8 10           0          0     TRUE
sched$critical_path
#> [1] "A" "B" "D"
